label: Proper being, internal unity, common…: Proper being is each thing’s own esse
term: proper being, internal unity, common numerical source and proper God in SCG I42[17–24]
definition: Proper being is each thing’s own esse. Internal unity concerns distinction within divine nature; numerical common-source unity concerns one source for all things. Proper divine being differs from dependent beings equivocally called gods and from divine-person distinctions.
note: One own esse per thing is not automatically one common esse; greatest internal unity is not external numerical uniqueness. The agreement-to-one-source rule and its application to being require independent warrant and cannot be silently identified with Anselm through/self-power policies. Governance analogy and doctrinal confession add no actual root or source-role dictionary.
